This challenge explores all matches of Italian soccer Serie A league from 1993 to current year. The dataset is contained in the website [football-data.co.uk](http://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php). 

### Challenges
1. Think about how to scrape the data from the website, but write no code at this stage.

Dobbiamo per ogni stagione della serie A presente nel sito prendere i dataset correlati e poi unirli in un unico grande dataset. Dobbiamo dunque prima ottenere i link dei file csv e poi leggerli.

1. Ask AI to write code to import data by scraping the website. Select only columns Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG (home team goals), FTAG (away team goals)  and filter rows with a valid (not NA) Date. 
```{r}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# seasons from 1993/94 to 2026/27, coded as "9394", ..., "0001", ..., "2627"
years <- 1993:2026
first_year <- years %% 100
second_year <- (years + 1) %% 100
first_year <- ifelse(first_year < 10, paste("0", first_year, sep = ""), first_year)
second_year <- ifelse(second_year < 10, paste("0", second_year, sep = ""), second_year)
seasons <- paste(first_year, second_year, sep = "")

# one CSV file per season
urls <- paste("https://www.football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/", seasons, "/I1.csv", sep = "")

# read one season and keep only the useful columns
read_season <- function(url) {
  read_csv(url) |>
    select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG)
}

# read all seasons, bind them and keep rows with a valid date
serieA <- lapply(urls, read_season) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  filter(!is.na(Date))

serieA
```

3. Using dplyr and tidyr packages (no for loops!), compute statistics for every team (matches, wins, loses, draws, points, points per match). Hint: mutate a column with the outcome of the match (for instance, H = home teams wins, A = away team wins, P = draw). Then group by team and outcome (home and away) and hence spread the outcome. Do this step without the use of AI.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

team_stats <- serieA |>
  mutate(outcome = ifelse(FTHG > FTAG, "H", ifelse(FTHG < FTAG, "A", "P"))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(HomeTeam, AwayTeam), names_to = "side", values_to = "team") |>
  group_by(team, side, outcome) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(wins  = ifelse(side == "HomeTeam", H, A),
         loses = ifelse(side == "HomeTeam", A, H),
         draws = P) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(wins = sum(wins), draws = sum(draws), loses = sum(loses)) |>
  mutate(matches = wins + draws + loses,
         points  = 3 * wins + draws,
         points_match   = points / matches) |>
  arrange(desc(points))

team_stats
```

4. Come up with at least 3 data questions on the data at hand. Just write the questions, do not find the answers.

Qual è il parametro che ci permette di dire qual è la migliore squadra italiana migliore di sempre? Le vittore? I punti? Il numero di gol fatti?

Quanti punti servono in media per vincere il campionato?

Quanti punti, invece, servono in media per non retrocedere in serie b?
